author: Evan Bales
title: Skeletal remains found under Greene County home could date back centuries - NewsBreak
text: DAYTON, Ohio ( WDTN ) — The examination of human remains found below a Greene County home has concluded. WDTN.com reported in April that remains were found under a Xenia Township home when replacing a porch. While the remains were “highly fragmented and incomplete,” the Greene County Coroner’s Office got to work identifying the individual. Officials used dental analysis to determine the person died well over 100 years ago. “They represent a historical time frame, sometime from the 1600s to the 1900s,” said Kevin Sharrett, Greene County coroner. “They’re not caveman bones, but these are old bones.” Because the remains only included a partial skeleton, the office could not conduct a full biological profile. The coroner consulted with experts from Montgomery County and even as far away as Delaware. In July, the remains were sent to Mercyhurst’s forensic anthropology lab in Erie, Pennsylvania. “There wasn’t a complete excavation, and not a whole lot of contextual information, just six to ten bones,” said Dr. Dennis Dirkmaat, Mercyhurt retired professor of forensic anthropology. The lab analyzed several elements, such as the stains of soil on the bones, the wear and tear on the few teeth discovered, and the size of the two leg bones — a tibia and femur. Using those clues, they were able to determine the bones likely belonged to a middle-aged man that died 100-400 years ago. “Though our analysis was limited, we were able to provide them with some pretty good clues as to the relative age of this individual,” said Dirkmaat. Officials were able to determine these bones did not come from any missing persons cases. With nobody to claim the remains, the bones will be stored until a future need arises. Sharrett says there isn’t enough information to determine a probably cause of death, but noted a black powder mill explosion in the 1880s, where 25 tons of gunpowder exploded, killing three and sending some remains as far as two miles away. However, the investigation has come to a close, and many questions will remain unanswered. For the latest news, weather, sports, and streaming video, head to Fox 8 Cleveland WJW.
